interface.title: Actigraphy (sleep log app for GGIR output)
interface.stage_of_work: Quality control and manual correction of automated outputs, before downstream GGIR sleep analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Shows each night of a participant's wrist-worn sensor data so a researcher can correct GGIR's predicted sleep onset and offset, mark extra sleep periods, exclude nights with too much missing data, and flag nights for review, with every change saved automatically.

data.note: The built-in demo participant at /work/app/paper/data/ggir_outputs/output_sub001, the only option in the dropdown. It has 3 nights, 1–3 May 2024: night 1 is a plain 23:00–07:00 window; night 2 already has a 13:00–14:00 nap window and the multiple-sleep switch on, with non-wear bands at about 00:00–01:00 and from about 22:30; night 3 has a non-wear band at about 22:30–00:00 and the missing-data switch already on. Edits are saved on the server. After this run the saved state is: night 1 flagged for review, window back to 23:00–07:00; night 2 nap ends at 14:31; night 3 onset 00:00 and flagged for review.

features.name: Time-series viewer with draggable interval range slider
features.general: Show a 24-hour signal trace with a shaded interval laid over it; drag the two handles of a range slider under the plot (or use arrow keys for one-minute steps) to move the start and end; the shading and a table of start, end and duration update at once and are saved
features.specific: Drag the onset/offset handles under the z-angle/arm-movement graph; the red 'sleep window' band and the Sleep Times table (Onset, Offset, Duration) update and auto-save
steps: Look at the trace and the shaded sleep window
Drag the onset handle to where the rest period actually starts
Drag the offset handle to where it ends
Fine-tune with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (1-minute steps)
Read the new onset, offset and duration in the Sleep Times table
serves_tasks: Correct the start and end of the main sleep period and see the corrected times next to the automatic ones
Inspect the signal for one night

features.name: Automatic vs. corrected interval tables
features.general: Show the algorithm's interval in a fixed reference table above an editable table of the user's corrected intervals, one row per interval, with sortable columns
features.specific: The 'GGIR Time' table (read-only) above the 'Sleep Times' table, which follows every slider; the Sleep Onset/Offset/Duration columns sort
steps: Read GGIR's predicted onset/offset
Edit the windows with the sliders
Compare the Sleep Times rows with the GGIR row
Optionally sort Sleep Times by onset
serves_tasks: Correct the start and end of the main sleep period and see the corrected times next to the automatic ones
Sort the list of corrected sleep periods

features.name: Add/remove extra intervals on one timeline
features.general: Add more range sliders to mark extra intervals on the same day; each new one starts as a zero-length interval, is kept from overlapping the others, and shows as its own shaded band and table row; remove the most recently added. Removing the last one leaves the day with no interval, which excludes that day from downstream analysis
features.specific: Add Slider creates a 12:00–12:00 window to drag open (naps, extra sleep periods); Remove Slider removes the last one; a night with no windows goes into data_cleaning night_part4 (per the code); the sleeplog file takes the longest window of each day as the main sleep
steps: Press Add Slider
Drag the new slider's handles to the nap's start and end
Turn on 'Are there multiple sleep periods in these data?'
Check the extra band on the graph and the extra row in Sleep Times
Press Remove Slider to delete the latest window
serves_tasks: Mark more than one sleep period in a day, then delete one
Record that a day has several sleep periods
Exclude a night from the sleep analysis by leaving it with no sleep period, or redraw one to bring it back

features.name: Day stepper that keeps each day's state
features.general: Step through the days of a recording with a stepped slider (click a mark or use arrow keys); each day's intervals and settings are kept and restored when you come back to it
features.specific: The 'Select day for participant sub001' slider; night 1's corrected window and review flag were still there on return (screens/024.webp)
steps: Pick a night with the day slider
Make corrections on that night
Move to another night
Come back and check the corrections and switches were kept
serves_tasks: Move between nights of the recording

features.name: Per-day yes/no quality flags
features.general: Set yes/no switches for each day; a switch can start already set from the data (a night with a non-wear gap opens with the missing-data flag on). Some flags change the analysis (exclude the day), others are only reminders
features.specific: 'Are >2 hours of data missing between 8PM to 8AM?' adds the night to data_cleaning night_part4 and drops it from GGIR sleep analysis; 'Do you need to review this night?' is stored only in the database (is_reviewed); green non-wear bands on the graph show the evidence
steps: Look for non-wear (green) bands or odd signal on the night
Turn on the missing-data switch to exclude the night
Turn on the review switch to remind yourself to come back
serves_tasks: Flag a night for later review (a reminder only; it does not change the analysis)
Exclude a night with too much missing data from the sleep analysis

features.name: Auto-saved annotation session
features.general: Every edit is written to the server straight away with no save button; moving between days or reopening the data source restores all saved intervals and flags

steps: Make edits on several nights
Move away and back to check they are kept

Step through nights and check the edits are there
